{
  "architecture_summary": "GoatOS is a large-scale, full-stack livestock farm management platform built on a hexagonal (ports-and-adapters) architecture in its Go backend, comprising 40+ bounded-context modules under backend/internal, each cleanly separated into domain, app, ports, and adapters layers. This backend serves four distinct frontend surfaces: a Next.js admin-web dashboard for operational management and CEO AI chat, a native Android application for offline-first field data capture with RFID and media proof integration, a lighter operator-mobile app, and a read-only investor analytics dashboard. Core business domains span Animal Health & Care (identity, vaccination, preventive care), Feed Management (direction generation, config, distribution), Field Operations (tasks, weighing, counts, pen visits), and Procurement & Supply Chain (vendors, inventory, sales). These are underpinned by two critical supporting domains: Verification & Process Integrity (proof capture, SOPs, audit, protocol adherence) which certifies data quality across all field workflows, and a Notification & Event Infrastructure domain implementing the transactional outbox pattern for reliable, loosely-coupled cross-domain communication via Pub/Sub. A standout capability is the Leadership Analytics & AI Assistant domain, which combines a Cube.js OLAP semantic layer with a Vertex AI-backed orchestrator that decomposes questions, executes guarded read-only tools, and synthesizes grounded answers for executives. Platform infrastructure (auth, observability, Postgres access via pgx/sqlc, task queues) is centralized in backend/internal/platform and consumed uniformly across all bounded contexts. The system integrates with Firebase (auth, push, distribution), Google Cloud (BigQuery, Pub/Sub, Cloud Tasks, GCS), MQTT/UDP IoT bridges for herd signals, and Grafana for observability. Overall the architecture demonstrates strong domain-driven decomposition with consistent structural patterns (domain/app/ports/adapters) repeated across nearly all backend modules, though the sheer number of fine-grained bounded contexts (40+) introduces significant coordination complexity, partially mitigated by the shared platform and event-bus infrastructure.",

### Workflow Research Report
Contains static analysis results of the codebase and business process analysis.

```json
"# System Workflow Analysis\n\n## 1. Main Workflow\n\n- **Workflow Name**: Field Task Execution & Proof Verification Flow\n\n- **Description**: This is the core operational workflow of GoatOS, connecting field-level data capture with backend verification and business process completion. Field operators use the Android app to identify animals via RFID, execute assigned tasks (feed distribution, preventive care, vaccination, etc.), and capture photo/video proof of completion. Data is persisted locally first (offline-first design) and synced to the backend via a transactional outbox pattern. The backend then routes submissions through a verification/sampling review process before marking the associated task complete, ensuring both operational continuity in low-connectivity environments and strong data integrity guarantees. This workflow underpins nearly all other business processes (vaccination, feed distribution, weighing, counts) since they all rely on the same capture-sync-verify pattern.\n\n- **Flow Diagram**:\n```mermaid\ngraph TD\n    Start[Operator Opens Task] --> ScanRfid[Scan Animal RFID Tag via Keyboard Wedge Reader]\n    ScanRfid --> CaptureProof[Capture Proof Media - Photo or Video via ViewModel]\n    CaptureProof --> RecordState[Record Task Completion State Locally]\n    RecordState --> PersistOutbox[Persist to Local Outbox Database]\n    PersistOutbox --> CheckConnectivity{Connectivity Available?}\n    CheckConnectivity -->|No| WaitRetry[Wait and Retry Sync Later]\n    WaitRetry --> CheckConnectivity\n    CheckConnectivity -->|Yes| SyncBackend[Sync Submission to Backend]\n    SyncBackend --> StoreProof[Backend Stores Proof Media - proof module]\n    StoreProof --> QueueVerification[Queue Submission for Verification Review]\n    QueueVerification --> ReviewDecision{Verification Passed?}\n    ReviewDecision -->|No| FlagRework[Flag for Rework or Rejection]\n    FlagRework --> NotifyOperator[Notify Operator via Notification Service]\n    NotifyOperator --> Start\n    ReviewDecision -->|Yes| MarkComplete[Mark Task Complete in Workboard]\n    MarkComplete --> PublishEvent[Publish Domain Event via Outbox]\n    PublishEvent --> End[Task Lifecycle Closed]\n```\n\n- **Key Steps**:\n  1. **RFID Scan** (`KeyboardWedgeRfidReader.kt`) – Identifies the target animal via Bluetooth HID keyboard-wedge integration.\n  2. **Proof Capture & State Recording** (`FeedDistributionCompleteViewModel.kt`, `PcCareTaskViewModel.kt`) – Captures photo/video evidence and manages multi-step task completion state.\n  3. **Local Persistence & Outbox Sync** (core-database / OutboxDatabase) – Ensures offline resilience; data is queued locally and synced when connectivity resumes.\n  4. **Backend Proof Storage** (`backend/internal/proof`) – Receives and durably stores media evidence (GCS/local).\n  5. **Verification Review** (`backend/internal/verification`) – Applies sampling/review rules to certify submission accuracy and protocol compliance.\n  6. **Task Completion & Event Publishing** (`backend/internal/tasks`, `backend/internal/outbox`) – Finalizes task status and emits domain events for downstream consumers (notifications, analytics).\n\n---\n\n## 2. Other Important Workflows\n\n### 2.1 Feed Direction Generation & Distribution Flow\n\n- **Description**: The backend generates daily feed direction sheets by combining shed scope filtering, feed configuration snapshots, and grain projections into an in-memory generation pipeline. Sheets progress through an issue → amend → lock lifecycle, with field distribution proof feeding back into the loop, and results surfaced to managers via the admin web dashboard.\n\n- **Flow Diagram**:\n```mermaid\ngraph TD\n    A[Trigger: Scheduled Job or Manual Issue] --> B[Filter Shed Scope - service.go]\n    B --> C[Batch Read Feed Config Snapshot - feedconfig]\n    C --> D[Generate In-Memory Feed Direction Rows via Grain Projection]\n    D --> E[Issue Sheet - lifecycle.go]\n    E --> F{Amendment Needed?}\n    F -->|Yes| G[Amend Sheet]\n    G --> E\n    F -->|No| H[Lock Sheet - Freeze Rows]\n    H --> I[Field Operator Distributes Feed]\n    I --> J[Capture Distribution Proof - proof module]\n    J --> K[Serve Frozen Rows for Reporting]\n    K --> L[Admin Web Displays Feed Direction Status]\n```\n\n### 2.2 Vaccination Program Execution Flow\n\n- **Description**: A vaccination plan defined in admin web drives generation of per-animal/cohort obligations. Field operators execute doses with RFID scanning and proof capture, submissions are verified, and eligibility/drive rollups are recomputed to feed back into analytics.\n\n- **Flow Diagram**:\n```mermaid\ngraph TD\n    A[Admin Defines Vaccination Plan & Cohort Matrix] --> B[Generate Vaccination Obligations]\n    B --> C[Operator Executes Dose with RFID Scan]\n    C --> D[Capture Proof of Administration]\n    D --> E[Verification Review for Compliance]\n    E --> F{Compliant?}\n    F -->|No| G[Flag for Correction]\n    G --> C\n    F -->|Yes| H[Recompute Drive & Eligibility Rollups]\n    H --> I[Expose Vaccination Coverage Metrics via Cube Analytics]\n```\n\n### 2.3 CEO AI Leadership Query Flow\n\n- **Description**: Executives interact with a conversational AI assistant to ask business questions. The orchestrator decomposes the query, executes bounded read-only tools against the Cube analytics layer and domain services, then synthesizes a grounded, safety-reviewed answer streamed back to the chat UI.\n\n- **Flow Diagram**:\n```mermaid\ngraph TD\n    A[User Submits Question in CEO AI Chat Panel] --> B[Orchestrator Decomposes Question into Sub-Questions]\n    B --> C[Plan Tool Calls]\n    C --> D[Execute Tools with Rate Limiting & SQL Guard]\n    D --> E[Query Cube Measures - Census/Mortality/Financial]\n    E --> F[Aggregate Tool Results]\n    F --> G[Synthesize Answer with Grounding Verification]\n    G --> H[Safety Review Pass]\n    H --> I{Passed Safety/Grounding?}\n    I -->|No| J[Return Fallback / Clarification]\n    I -->|Yes| K[Stream Final Answer to Chat UI]\n```\n\n### 2.4 Investor Analytics Reporting Flow\n\n- **Description**: Investors access a read-only dashboard that fetches aggregated metrics (mortality, counts, feed cost, births) from backend/cube APIs, sharing the same Cube.js semantic layer used by the CEO AI assistant, ensuring consistent metric definitions across leadership-facing surfaces.\n\n- **Flow Diagram**:\n```mermaid\ngraph TD\n    A[Investor Navigates to Dashboard Page] --> B[Fetch Aggregated Analytics via API Route]\n    B --> C[Resolve Cube Query Against Canonical Animal/Location Data]\n    C --> D[Map Results into Typed Domain Models]\n    D --> E[Render Visualization on Dashboard]\n```\n\n### 2.5 Procurement to Sales Value Chain Flow\n\n- **Description**: Vendor feed/resource purchases are recorded and reconciled against inventory consumption, ultimately linking to animal/product sales for farm-value reporting. Domain events are published via the outbox for downstream notification and analytics consumption.\n\n- **Flow Diagram**:\n```mermaid\ngraph TD\n    A[Record Vendor Source-Entry Load] --> B[Reconcile Inventory Batch]\n    B --> C[Record Animal/Product Sale]\n    C --> D[Compute Farm Value]\n    D --> E[Publish Domain Events via Outbox]\n    E --> F[Display Procurement/Sales Analytics on Admin Web]\n```\n\n### 2.6 App Bootstrap & Offline-First Initialization Flow (Android)\n\n- **Description**: On launch, the Android app initializes through a bootstrap state machine (Loading/Ready/Error), applying cached identity data, refreshing navigation state, and handling force-update logic before presenting the main navigation shell to the operator.\n\n- **Flow Diagram**:\n```mermaid\ngraph TD\n    A[App Launch - MainActivity] --> B[BootstrapViewModel: Loading State]\n    B --> C[Load Bootstrap Cache from Room DB]\n    C --> D[Apply Authentication Identity]\n    D --> E{Force Update Required?}\n    E -->|Yes| F[Download & Install APK Update]\n    F --> A\n    E -->|No| G[Refresh Navigation State]\n    G --> H[Transition to Ready State]\n    H --> I[Render GoatOsShell Navigation]\n```\n\n---\n\n## 3. Workflow Insights\n\n- **Unified Capture-Verify-Sync Pattern**: Nearly all field-level business processes (feed distribution, preventive care, vaccination execution, pen visits, weighing, counts) converge on the same underlying pattern: RFID/data capture → proof media → local outbox persistence → backend sync → verification review → completion. This consistency (validated by the Verification & Process Integrity domain acting as a shared supporting service) significantly reduces duplication of quality-control logic across business domains, though it also means any defect in the outbox/verification pipeline has wide blast radius.\n\n- **Shared Analytics Backbone Across Leadership Surfaces**: Both the CEO AI Orchestrator and the Investor Analytics Dashboard depend on the same Cube.js semantic layer (`animals.yml` and related cube definitions). This ensures metric consistency between conversational AI answers and static dashboards, but also creates a tight coupling point — any change to cube measure definitions (explicitly documented as a \"governed contract\") must be carefully versioned to avoid breaking both consumers simultaneously.\n\n- **Thin Orchestration, Rich Domain Logic**: The Feed Direction service (`service.go`, `lifecycle.go`) exemplifies a deliberate architectural pattern of \"thin orchestration with bounded reads\" — separating pure in-memory generation logic from the issue/amend/lock lifecycle state machine. This pattern of orchestrator + lifecycle separation appears to be a reusable template that could be extended to other generation-heavy domains (e.g., vaccination obligation generation, growth direction).\n\n- **Offline-First as a Cross-Cutting Design Constraint**: The Android app's reliance on Room database caching (bootstrap_cache across multiple schema versions v28–v63) and outbox-based sync reflects a deliberate design choice to support intermittent connectivity in rural farm environments. This adds engineering complexity (schema migrations, sync conflict handling) but is essential given the target user base of field operators.\n\n- **Verification as a Cross-Domain Gatekeeper**: The Verification & Process Integrity domain does not own primary business data but acts as a mandatory checkpoint gating task completion across Animal Health, Feed Management, and Field Operations domains. This creates a strong but potentially bottlenecking dependency — verification review latency directly impacts operational throughput across multiple workflows.\n\n- **Event-Driven Decoupling via Outbox**: The Notification & Event Infrastructure domain (outbox pattern, domain event consumer, Pub/Sub relay) is consistently used as the integration mechanism between Procurement/Sales, Field Operations, and Notification domains, avoiding direct synchronous coupling. This is a sound architectural choice for reliability but introduces eventual-consistency considerations that are not always explicit in the UI (e.g., dashboard staleness).\n\n- **Potential Optimization Opportunity**: The Feed Direction, Vaccination, and Preventive Care workflows independently implement similar \"generate obligations/sheets → execute in field → verify → recompute rollups\" cycles. Given the shared platform infrastructure, extracting a common \"scheduled obligation lifecycle\" abstraction could reduce duplicated logic across `feeddirection`, `vaccination`, and `pccare` modules.\n\n- **Dependency Chain Risk**: Both the CEO AI flow and Investor dashboard flow terminate in Cube.js queries against canonical `animals`/`locations` tables — meaning upstream data quality issues in identity, counts, or health records propagate directly into leadership-facing analytics without an explicit intermediate validation layer, relying instead on the general Verification domain upstream."

      "summary": "This directory contains multiple file groups. It contains React components, server actions, and utilities organized around three main features: Herd Analytics (composition and movement tracking), Counts Breakdown (detailed census by stage/breed/gender/shed), and Herd Register (individual animal records). The files work together through shared data types, filtering mechanisms, and coordinated server actions to provide a complete inventory management system. The \"counts\" directory contains frontend and server-side components for managing animal counts and pen operations in an agricultural admin interface. The files implement a coordinated workflow combining interactive cell editing (inline-cell-editor.tsx), data management pages (milk-preparation.tsx), pen-level operations (shed-stage-actions.ts, shed-tag-editor.tsx), and validation utilities.       "summary": "This directory contains multiple file groups. Key aspects: This directory contains a comprehensive collection of Android ViewModel classes implementing the MVVM architecture pattern for feed-related user workflows. The ViewModels manage state, coordinate with repositories/services, and expose reactive streams (StateFlow, LiveData) to UI layers across multiple feed operations including distribution, packing, purchases, transport, and wastage management. The \"viewmodel\" directory contains 75 Kotlin ViewModels that serve as the presentation layer in the MVVM architecture for the Goatos Android application. These files manage UI state, handle user interactions through event systems, and coordinate with repositories and services to fetch/manipulate data. The ViewModels cover various business domains including health tracking, leadership tasks, leave management, milk feeding/preparation, and preventive care planning, each following a consistent pattern of state management using Kotlin Flow and lifecycle awareness through Android Architecture Components. The viewmodel directory contains Android ViewModel classes that manage state and business logic for various features in the GoatOS application. These ViewModels handle event processing, data binding, UI state management, and coordinate with repositories and services. The files work together as a presentation layer, implementing reactive patterns using Kotlin Flow and coroutines for consistent state management across preventive care, pen reconciliation, and visit detail features. The viewmodel directory contains core UI state management ViewModels for the Goatos Android application, including specialized ViewModels for RFID scanning, sales pipeline management, and sales transactions. These ViewModels implement the MVVM architecture pattern, handling business logic, event processing, and state management for various feature screens using Kotlin coroutines and reactive flows. The viewmodel directory contains Android ViewModels that manage UI state and business logic for various features in the GoatOS application, including livestock management (shifting), vaccination tracking (sheds), and task submission. These ViewModels follow the MVVM pattern, using Kotlin coroutines and StateFlow for reactive state management, coordinating data from repositories, services, and APIs while exposing UI-ready state to activities/fragments. The batch includes 9 key ViewModels that handle complex workflows like animal shifting operations, vaccination execution tracking, task completion, and data synchronization. The \"viewmodel\" directory contains Android ViewModel components that manage UI state and business logic for the Goatos livestock management application. These ViewModels use Kotlin coroutines and reactive flows to maintain and expose application state, specifically handling weighing, fasting, planning, and shed management features. The directory serves as a critical bridge between UI layers and business logic, implementing the MVVM architectural pattern with dependency injection via Hilt.\n\n The viewmodel directory (batch 9/10) contains Android ViewModel classes implementing the MVVM architecture pattern using Kotlin and Jetpack Compose. These ViewModels manage UI state, handle user interactions, and coordinate with business logic layers for features like weighing tasks, work board management, and detailed work board operations. The files demonstrate sophisticated state management using Kotlin coroutines, LiveData/StateFlow, and reactive patterns to support complex Android applications. The viewmodel directory contains critical ViewModel classes that manage the presentation logic and state for Android workflow-related features in the Goatos application. The two major ViewModels (WorkflowDetailViewModel and WorkflowListViewModel) handle complex business workflows including workflow detail management, pagination, filtering, evidence capture, and date-based navigation, serving as essential controller components that bridge the UI and business logic layers."

      "summary": "This directory contains multiple file groups. Key aspects: The postgres directory contains data access layer (DAO) and repository implementations for the goats backend counting/herd management system, providing database-backed operations for alerts, breeds, approvals, milk feeding/preparation, and herd analytics. These files work together to expose domain business logic through PostgreSQL queries, handling both read operations (querying herd state, analytics) and write operations (approvals, milk records, pen reconciliation). The directory represents a critical data layer that bridges domain business rules with persistent storage, serving operational needs for farm management across multiple functional areas. The postgres directory is a data access layer (DAO) implementation for the Counts and Shifting subsystems, providing persistence operations for managing animal counts and movement/shifting workflows over PostgreSQL. It owns critical business logic including approval workflows, feed requirements calculation, execution tracking, and destination management for the operator-facing shifting (movement) functionality, using direct SQL queries and pgx for database interactions."

      "summary": "This directory contains multiple file groups. Key aspects: The postgres directory contains the PostgreSQL data access layer for the weighing domain within the goatos backend system. These files implement adapters that handle domain-specific operations including alerts, campaigns, closures, exports, fasting schedules, growth calculations, and weight tracking - serving as the persistence layer between business logic and the database with comprehensive support for reporting, auditing, and domain constraints. This postgres batch contains core data access layer (DAO) files implementing the weighing domain's reporting and oversight surfaces. The files handle bucket-grain leadership pagination, load-weight calculations, operator summaries, cohort filtering (by origin and proof status), park vocabularies, and shared reporting scope definitions. Together, they provide the backend's tally and filtering infrastructure for the Weights screen and oversight surfaces, with careful attention to weighing isolation rules and data integrity guards. The postgres directory contains data access layer (DAO) components that handle PostgreSQL database operations for the weighing domain. These files implement critical business logic for managing weighing observations, shed partitions, rework verdicts, and sex scoping—serving as the persistence layer that bridges domain models with the database. The files work together to provide repository patterns, SQL query builders, and data transformation logic specific to the weighing and tracking operations. This is batch 4/4 of the postgres package containing core weighing domain logic and data persistence operations. The files implement the complete weighing workflow including weight recording, verification, correction, historical tracking, and various reporting/analytics queries against the PostgreSQL database. These files serve as the primary data access and business logic layer for the weighing campaign system, handling shed partitions, submission events, weight demographics, and verification verdicts."

      "summary": "The workboard directory serves as a cross-module Work Board abstraction layer that provides a unified, normalized interface for operational data across different modules.
